rationale: Last of the three items the gap named: restarts are now an event in the sweep. A restart event picks a node, writes what an application would have persisted - the node's hard state through SetHardState, and its applied ConfState into the storage's snapshot metadata - then re-creates the raft instance with newRaft over that storage and Config.Applied set to the node's applied index, and re-registers it with the network. Both supplied pieces come from the knowledge established earlier: newRaft reads the configuration only from Storage.InitialState's ConfState and MemoryStorage never tracks it, and a restart without the hard state would silently lose term and vote. Draft-side this revision reports invariant_sweep_summary with seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=466, ordinary proposals=452, conf_change_proposals=249, restarts=471 and violations=0, so the four invariants still show no witness with restarting nodes in the event set - including the committed-index monotonicity check, which is the one a restart could most plausibly break if the restarted node came back with a lower commit index. That is construction feedback only, so the experiment below requests isolated execution of these bytes. One gap item remains unbuilt after this: the liveness witness for the campaign guard's applied-lag condition, and a demotion of an existing serving voter is still not proposed, so the gap stays open.

scope.description: Seventh revision of the same fixed harness; probes A, B and C are unchanged. The sweep (four real state machines, ids 1..4, node 4 registered directly with the network and starting outside the configuration; configuration events proposing single changes on node 4 half of the time with Transition=JointImplicit; committed conf changes applied through applyConfChange) now also restarts a randomly chosen node: it persists the node's hard state via SetHardState, copies the node's applied ConfState into the storage snapshot metadata, then rebuilds the instance with newRaft over that storage with Config.Applied set to the node's applied index and re-registers it with the network. The four invariants (at most one leader per term, committed (index,term) consistency, committed-index monotonicity per node, applied<=committed) are still checked after every event and invariant_sweep_summary now also reports the number of restarts. The liveness witness for committed-but-unapplied conf changes is still not recorded, and configuration changes still concern node 4 only.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, SetHardState, newRaft); no production logic is modified.

The restart supplies exactly what the application is documented to persist - hard state and the ConfState it last applied - so the restarted instance starts from the configuration the target reads in Storage.InitialState rather than from an assumed one.
Config.Applied is set to the node's applied index, which is what the application would report on restart.
Randomness is fixed per seed; absence of violations is a holds-only result for this event set, not a safety proof.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup on a random node, MsgProp with a tagged payload, tick() on a random node, isolate a random node, recover, TransferLeader from a random voter to the current leader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change on node 4, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node from its persisted hard state and applied ConfState, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 and evaluate the four invariants, emitting a violation event with seed, step, nodes and operands when one is found, and finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary with seeds, steps, elections, proposals, conf_change_proposals, restarts and violations.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with a restart event added: a random node is rebuilt from its persisted hard state and applied ConfState through newRaft, which is the last item the open gap named for the event set. Fresh execution is requested because the harness bytes and the event set changed.
